sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜店打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍贵的藏品去上班，然后把DJ台变成这样一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面陈列着美丽而历经50年的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在，请在您最喜爱的播客平台上收听来自Audemars Piguet的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》的我叫迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: For decades, the world seemed to be winning the war against mosquitoes and the deadly diseases that they carry.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，世界似乎在与蚊子及其传播的致命疾病的战争中取得胜利。

sentences.en: Now, we're once again losing that battle.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们再次陷入了这场战役的劣势。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Stephanie Nolan explains why.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事斯蒂芬妮·诺兰将解释原因。

sentences.en: Thursday, October 5th.
sentences.zh: 10月5日，星期四。

sentences.en: Stephanie, you have embarked on an entire line of coverage for The Times about mosquitoes.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮，你为《纽约时报》开展了一整条关于蚊子的报道线。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why mosquitoes?
sentences.zh: 为什么是蚊子？

sentences.en: And why now?
sentences.zh: 又为什么是现在？

sentences.en: So, I went into this really thinking about solutions.
sentences.zh: 所以，我开始做这个的时候其实是想着寻找解决方案的。

sentences.en: I was going to do some nerdy, geeky stories because I knew there was some great new technology coming to fight mosquitoes.
sentences.zh: 我本来打算做一些书呆子气、极客风格的报道，因为我知道有一些应对蚊子的伟大新技术即将问世。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're our biggest enemy, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，它们是我们最大的敌人，对吧？

sentences.en: They're the deadliest animal.
sentences.zh: 它们是最致命的动物。

sentences.en: Well, just explain that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，请解释一下这个。

sentences.en: They're the deadliest animal.
sentences.zh: 它们是最致命的动物。

sentences.en: So, they kill more humans than anything else, than any other living creature.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们杀死的人类比任何其他东西、比任何其他生物都多。

sentences.en: Because of the diseases that they carry.
sentences.zh: 因为它们传播的疾病。

sentences.en: Because of the diseases they carry.
sentences.zh: 因为它们传播的疾病。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's West Nile.
sentences.zh: 有西尼罗河病毒。

sentences.en: There's dengue.
sentences.zh: 有登革热。

sentences.en: There's malaria.
sentences.zh: 有疟疾。

sentences.en: So, I went into this planning to look at solutions.
sentences.zh: 所以，我一开始是计划着寻找解决方案的。

sentences.en: And really quickly, I realized that I hadn't really kept up with the scale of the problem.
sentences.zh: 但很快，我意识到自己并没有真正跟上问题严重性的规模。

sentences.en: That, yes, we have new tools, but we need them because the problem has really gotten away from us.
sentences.zh: 那就是，是的，我们有了新工具，但我们需要它们，因为问题已经真正失控了。

sentences.en: And I covered public health, global public health, for a living, but I hadn't realized how much the kind of tide in this battle had shifted that the mosquitoes were winning.
sentences.zh: 而且我一直以报道公共卫生、全球公共卫生为生，但我没有意识到这场战役的风向已经发生了多大的变化，蚊子正在获胜。

sentences.en: And winning how?
sentences.zh: 怎么个获胜法？

sentences.en: They're winning in terms of our ability to control mosquito-borne disease.
sentences.zh: 它们在控制蚊媒疾病的能力上正在获胜。

sentences.en: And the place where you see that the most strikingly, I think, is with malaria, with malaria in Africa.
sentences.zh: 我认为，表现得最显著的地方就是疟疾，非洲的疟疾。

sentences.en: We were doing a really good job of bringing down malaria deaths, and that progress has stopped.
sentences.zh: 我们原本在压低疟疾死亡人数方面做得很好，但这种进展已经停止了。

sentences.en: That is genuinely surprising to me because I think of malaria as a disease that we have mostly gotten under control.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到由衷的惊讶，因为我认为疟疾是一种我们基本已经控制住的疾病。

sentences.en: So, lay out for us exactly what happened and why that progress has stopped.
sentences.zh: 那么，请给我们详细讲讲到底发生了什么，以及为什么这种进展会停止。

sentences.en: So, if you go back, like, 20 years, almost a million people were dying of malaria every year.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你回溯大约20年前，每年有近百万人死于疟疾。

sentences.en: Almost all of them in Africa.
sentences.zh: 几乎全部在非洲。

sentences.en: So, just to remind you, the way that malaria spreads, right, is you have a mosquito who bites a person who has the parasite.
sentences.zh: 所以，提醒一下大家，疟疾传播的方式，对吧，就是有一只蚊子叮咬了一个携带寄生虫的人。

sentences.en: The parasite reproduces in the gut of the mosquito, and then when it bites the next person, that person gets infected.
sentences.zh: 寄生虫在蚊子的肠道内繁殖，然后当它叮咬下一个人的时候，那个人就被感染了。

sentences.en: And you have these cycles of sickness that go through families.
sentences.zh: 你就会看到这种在家庭成员中循环的疾病。

sentences.en: And it can be deadly, of course, especially for small children.
sentences.zh: 当然，这可能是致命的，尤其是对幼儿而言。

sentences.en: But it's not just about death, right?
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是关于死亡，对吧？

sentences.en: It's horrible.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.en: You get fevers that can be so severe.
sentences.zh: 你会经历非常剧烈的高烧。

sentences.en: You get hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 你会出现幻觉。

sentences.en: You get vomiting.
sentences.zh: 你会呕吐。

sentences.en: You get this absolutely debilitating fatigue.
sentences.zh: 你会感到这种绝对使人衰弱的疲劳。

sentences.en: And you don't get it once, right?
sentences.zh: 而且你不会只得一次，对吧？

sentences.en: You can get it four or five times in a rainy season.
sentences.zh: 在一个雨季里，你可能会得四到五次。

sentences.en: And kids are getting 10 cases in a year.
sentences.zh: 孩子们一年会得10次。

sentences.en: And that takes, like, a huge toll on their families.
sentences.zh: 这就像是对他们的家庭造成了巨大的沉重打击。

sentences.en: They're spending their money on medical bills, and people can't go to work because they're taking care of them.
sentences.zh: 他们把钱花在医疗账单上，人们因为要照顾他们而无法去工作。

sentences.en: There's a huge economic coSt.
sentences.zh: 有着巨大的经济代价。

sentences.en: And so for all of these reasons, in the late 1990s, there's a decision by African governments,
sentences.zh: 因此，基于所有这些原因，在20世纪90年代末，非洲各国政府做出了一个决定，

sentences.en: by some philanthropists and global public health organizations to really make an effort to wipe malaria out in Africa.
sentences.zh: 一些慈善家和全球公共卫生组织决定真正努力在非洲消灭疟疾。

sentences.en: We are, first of all, reaching out to other partners, making an alliance for rollback malaria.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们正在接触其他合作伙伴，建立一个遏制疟疾的联盟。

sentences.en: And what does that look like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样子的？

sentences.en: It's a big investment.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔巨大的投资。

sentences.en: Microsoft founder Bill Gates is giving up daily control of his company to concentrate on his foundation, which funds health and education projects worldwide.
sentences.zh: 微软创始人比尔·盖茨正放弃对公司的日常控制，以专注于他的基金会，该基金会资助全球的健康和教育项目。

sentences.en: A lot of that money comes from philanthropy, from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation in particular, who make eradicating malaria a huge priority.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分资金来自慈善事业，特别是比尔及梅琳达·盖茨基金会，他们将根除疟疾置于极其优先的地位。

sentences.en: The fact that it kills over a million children a year and yet has almost no money given to it, you know, that struck us as very strange.
sentences.zh: 它每年夺走一百多万儿童的生命，然而几乎没有获得资金投入，你知道的，这让我们觉得非常奇怪。

sentences.en: And the decision is to try three strategies.
sentences.zh: 于是决定的尝试三种策略。

sentences.en: We'll take the diseases of the poor, or there's no market, and we'll get the best scientists working on those diseases.
sentences.zh: 我们将针对穷人的疾病，或者那些没有市场的疾病，让最优秀的科学家来研究这些疾病。

sentences.en: One is better drugs.
sentences.zh: 一是更好的药物。

sentences.en: So there are new and better treatments for malaria, and there's a real effort to get those into primary health care clinics across rural Africa.
sentences.zh: 因此，有了更新更好的疟疾治疗方法，并且正在做出真正的努力，将这些药物送入整个非洲农村的初级卫生保健诊所。

sentences.en: There were also new and better insecticides.
sentences.zh: 还有更新更好的杀虫剂。

sentences.en: So in places with a heavy malaria burden, they would spray insecticides inside people's homes, and they're long-acting, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，在疟疾负担沉重的地方，他们会在人们的房屋内喷洒杀虫剂，而且它们是长效的，对吧？

sentences.en: And so that would provide you with protection for a while.
sentences.zh: 所以这会为你提供一段时间的保护。

sentences.en: And then the last one, bed nets.
sentences.zh: 然后最后一种，蚊帐。

sentences.en: The thinking was that the main mosquitoes that transmit malaria in Africa, they bite indoors and at night when people are asleep.
sentences.zh: 当时的设想是，在非洲传播疟疾的主力蚊子，它们是在室内和夜间人们睡觉时叮咬人的。

sentences.en: And that's when people are getting infected.
sentences.zh: 而那是人们被感染的时候。

sentences.en: And so you had this huge campaign to get an insecticide-treated bed net in every household, on every family.
sentences.zh: 因此，你们开展了一场大规模的运动，让每户人家、每个家庭都拥有一顶经过杀虫剂处理的蚊帐。

sentences.en: Mothers were sent home from clinics with them with their new babies.
sentences.zh: 母亲们带着新生儿从诊所回家时会领到蚊帐。

sentences.en: Trucks would roll into villages and give them out.
sentences.zh: 卡车会开进村庄把它们分发出去。

sentences.en: And so as these elements come together, I'm quite optimistic that we will be able to eradicate malaria.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着这些要素结合在一起，我相当乐观地认为我们将能够根除疟疾。

sentences.en: And how do these three solutions, including this quite low-tech bed net solution, actually work?
sentences.zh: 那么这三种解决方案，包括这种技术含量相当低的蚊帐解决方案，实际上是如何起作用的呢？

sentences.en: Well, it works really well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，效果非常好。

sentences.en: Deaths come way down.
sentences.zh: 死亡人数大幅下降。

sentences.en: Cases come way down.
sentences.zh: 病例大幅下降。

sentences.en: By about 2015, deaths bottomed out at about 550,000 people, which obviously is still a horrifying number of people.
sentences.zh: 到2015年左右，死亡人数触底，约为550,000人，这显然仍然是一个令人毛骨悚然的数字。

sentences.en: But you've cut deaths in half, right?
sentences.zh: 但你已经将死亡人数减少了一半，对吧？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And people have really seen the difference in their lives and the economic impact on their families.
sentences.zh: 人们确实看到了他们生活中的变化以及对他们家庭的经济影响。

sentences.en: And so for a while there, as you're watching that curve of infections come down, there's a belief that, like, okay, if we keep investing in this and we keep going,
sentences.zh: 所以在一段时间里，当你看着感染曲线下降时，人们会有一种信念，那就是，好吧，如果我们继续对此进行投资并坚持下去，

sentences.en: maybe we're going to get to elimination.
sentences.zh: 也许我们将能够实现消除。

sentences.en: So how do we get instead to where you say we are, which is not elimination, but instead mosquitoes and malaria resurgent and winning?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们是如何变成你所说的这种局面的——不是消除，而是蚊子和疟疾死灰复燃并正在取胜？

sentences.en: Well, so here's what I have found in my reporting after talking to dozens and dozens of malariologists, parasitologists, entomologists,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这就是我在采访了几十位甚至上百位疟疾学家、寄生虫学家、昆虫学家之后，在我的报道中发现的情况，

sentences.en: all kinds of people who were working in this all over Africa.
sentences.zh: 各种在全非洲各地从事这项工作的人。

sentences.en: The short answer is the mosquitoes adapted.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是：蚊子适应了。

sentences.en: Their lifespan might only be six or seven weeks, and they evolve really, really quickly.
sentences.zh: 它们的寿命可能只有六七周，而且它们进化得非常非常快。

sentences.en: So you get a lot of mutations within a mosquito, which means that there's lots of opportunities for a mosquito to develop a way that it can survive what we're throwing against it.
sentences.zh: 所以你在蚊子体内会得到很多突变，这意味着蚊子有很多机会开发出一种能够经受住我们对它们进行打击的方法。

sentences.en: And so really quickly, mosquitoes have outmaneuvered the solutions that we had in place.
sentences.zh: 因此，蚊子非常迅速地智胜了我们当时拥有的解决方案。

sentences.en: And one of the big changes ties directly to bed nets.
sentences.zh: 其中一个巨大的变化直接与蚊子有关。

sentences.en: So if mosquitoes were not able to feed at night, they weren't able to feed on sleepers who were under nets, some of those mosquitoes died out.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果蚊子无法在夜间进食，它们就无法在蚊帐下睡觉的人身上进食，其中一些蚊子就会消亡。

sentences.en: And there was an evolutionary advantage for those who started feeding at other times in other places.
sentences.zh: 而对于那些开始在其他时间和地点进食的蚊子来说，这是一种进化的优势。

sentences.en: And so now you have mosquitoes that are feeding outdoors, feeding during the daytime.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你有了在户外进食、在白天进食的蚊子。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And obviously, people are not wandering around all day long wrapped in a bed net, right?
sentences.zh: 显然，人们不会一整天都裹着蚊帐四处走动，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if you're not protected anymore at the time when those mosquitoes are biting, suddenly you have cases starting to go back up.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果在这些蚊子叮咬的时候你不再受到保护，突然之间你的病例又开始上升了。

sentences.en: And, you know, that same evolutionary advantage issue comes up with the treatments, and it comes up with the insecticides.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，治疗方法和杀虫剂也面临着同样的发展优势问题。

sentences.en: Mosquitoes are resistant at this point to almost all of the chemicals, all of the insecticides that are being used across Africa.
sentences.zh: 目前，蚊子对几乎所有的化学物质、全非洲正在使用的所有杀虫剂都产生了抗药性。

sentences.en: They just don't kill them the way they did 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 它们不像20年前那样能杀死它们了。

sentences.en: So those three very effective solutions you mentioned that really brought down death from malaria across Africa,
sentences.zh: 所以你提到的那三个非常有效的解决方案，确实使全非洲的疟疾死亡人数大幅下降，

sentences.en: they create the conditions in which these mosquitoes adapt and adapt in ways that outsmart all three of these solutions.
sentences.zh: 它们创造了这样一种条件：这些蚊子进行适应，并以智胜所有这三种解决方案的方式进行适应。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And brace yourself for this, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，做好心理准备吧。

sentences.en: It gets worse.
sentences.zh: 情况更糟了。

sentences.en: So I'm reporting on all of this, and I call up a scientist at the CDC who runs their entomology program, and she tells me, yes, these daytime biters,
sentences.zh: 所以我在报道所有这些事情，我打电话给疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）的一位科学家，她负责他们的昆虫学项目，她告诉我，是的，这些白天叮咬的蚊子，

sentences.en: these insecticide-resistant mosquitoes, it's all a really big problem.
sentences.zh: 这些具有抗药性的蚊子，这全都是一个非常大的问题。

sentences.en: But also, she says, that I've missed something huge.
sentences.zh: 但同时，她说，我漏掉了一个极其重要的事情。

sentences.en: Which is what?
sentences.zh: 是什么？

sentences.en: Well, while the public health world has been focused on mosquitoes and the way that they're adapting and how to respond to malaria in rural Africa, there's a whole new mosquito.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当公共卫生界一直专注于蚊子以及它们适应的方式以及如何在非洲农村应对疟疾时，出现了一种全新的蚊子。

sentences.en: And it's an urban mosquito.
sentences.zh: 它是一种城市蚊子。

sentences.en: It's highly adapted to live and thrive in cities.
sentences.zh: 它高度适应了在城市中生活和繁衍。

sentences.en: So suddenly there's a kind of double whammy nightmare scenario being presented to you.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，有一种双重打击的噩梦般的情景呈现在你面前。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Not only are mosquitoes out adapting all the tools that we had for rural malaria, now you have a mosquito that's bringing the disease into urban areas,
sentences.zh: 不仅蚊子超越适应了我们用于农村疟疾的所有工具，现在你还有了一种将疾病带入城市地区的蚊子，

sentences.en: and they're totally unprepared to respond.
sentences.zh: 而他们对此完全没有准备好应对。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So Stephanie, tell us more about this second threat, this mosquito that's now posing a risk to Africa's cities.
sentences.zh: 那么斯蒂芬妮，请跟我们多讲讲这个第二个威胁，这只现在正对非洲城市构成风险的蚊子。

sentences.en: So it's a mosquito called Anopheles.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种叫做按蚊的蚊子。

sentences.en: Well, here's where it gets tricky.
sentences.zh: 嗯，棘手的地方就在这里。

sentences.en: It's called Anopheles stevenzii, or Anopheles stevenzii, and the entomologists I've interviewed are kind of split right down the middle about how to pronounce it.
sentences.zh: 它被称为斯氏按蚊（Anopheles stephensi），我采访的昆虫学家对于如何发音意见几乎对半开。

sentences.en: And so, in fact, a lot of them now just refer to her as Steve.
sentences.zh: 因此，事实上，他们现在很多人只是简称她为史蒂夫（Steve）。

sentences.en: Turns out these folks have a pretty good sense of humor in the face of some pretty awful information.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，面对一些相当糟糕的信息时，这些家伙有着相当不错的幽默感。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And Steve, but we're using she, her, because mosquitoes, of course, the ones that bite us, are all the females who are in search of blood for the protein to lay eggs.
sentences.zh: 而史蒂夫——但我们使用的是“她”，因为蚊子，当然，那些叮咬我们的都是雌性，它们为了产卵所需的蛋白质而在寻找血液。

sentences.en: So Steve is, she's kind of the superhero of mosquitoes.
sentences.zh: 所以史蒂夫，她有点像是蚊子中的超级英雄。

sentences.en: She's unbelievably adaptable.
sentences.zh: 她拥有难以置信的适应能力。

sentences.en: She's great at high temperatures.
sentences.zh: 她非常适应高温。

sentences.en: She likes it when it's wet, but she's also fine when it's dry.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢潮湿，但也完全能适应干燥。

sentences.en: She'll breed all year round, so you're not talking about having a malaria season anymore, like in a rainy season.
sentences.zh: 她一年四季都会繁殖，所以你不再是在谈论像雨季那样的疟疾季节了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And on top of all of that, she's what, in the entomology world, they call a very competent vector, which means she's really good at spreading the malaria parasite.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，她在昆虫学界被称为一个“非常称职的媒介”，这意味着她非常擅长传播疟疾寄生虫。

sentences.en: It lives well inside her, and it's very easy for her to pass it on to the next person she bites.
sentences.zh: 它在她体内生活得很好，她非常容易把它传给下一个她叮咬的人。

sentences.en: So perhaps not a superhero, but instead, like, a villain.
sentences.zh: 所以或许不是超级英雄，而更像是个反派。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Is this one of the mosquitoes, Stephanie,
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮，这是不是那种蚊子，

sentences.en: that we think evolved across rural Africa during this period when bed nets and insecticides were being used and just has found her way into cities?
sentences.zh: 我们认为在蚊帐和杀虫剂被使用的这段时间里，它在整个非洲农村进化，然后刚刚找到了进入城市的途径？

sentences.en: Great question, but no.
sentences.zh: 问得好，但不是。

sentences.en: Steve is an immigrant.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫是一个移民。

sentences.en: She originates in South Asia, in India and Pakistan, unknown in Africa until way back in 2012.
sentences.zh: 她源自南亚，在印度和巴基斯坦，直到遥远的2012年在非洲才为人所知。

sentences.en: So in 2012, it was found in the tiny little country of Djibouti on the Horn of Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以在2012年，它在非洲之角的吉布提这个微型国家被发现。

sentences.en: And the theory is that she was imported on container ships, maybe in old car tires.
sentences.zh: 有一种理论认为，她是通过集装箱货船被输入进来的，也许藏在旧汽车轮胎里。

sentences.en: And, you know, initially, nobody was overly concerned about this until all of a sudden in Djibouti City, malaria cases started to creep up.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，最初并没有人对此过分担心，直到突然之间在吉布提市，疟疾病例开始攀升。

sentences.en: And remember, malaria is not known as an urban disease, right?
sentences.zh: 请记住，疟疾不被称为城市疾病，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, we're talking about a rural disease when we talk about malaria in Africa.
sentences.zh: 就像我们在谈论非洲的疟疾时，我们讨论的是一种农村疾病。

sentences.en: So it caused a lot of confusion.
sentences.zh: 所以这引起了很大的困惑。

sentences.en: Like, what exactly is going on in Djibouti?
sentences.zh: 比如，吉布提到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: And then in 2022, you get an outbreak of malaria in Ethiopia's second largest city, which is a place called Diradawa.
sentences.zh: 然后到了2022年，埃塞俄比亚第二大城市德雷达瓦爆发了疟疾。

sentences.en: And it's got about a half a million people.
sentences.zh: 那里大约有五十万人口。

sentences.en: And what happens is that at Diradawa University, which ends up being the center of this outbreak, half of the students who live in the male dormitories fall ill.
sentences.zh: 情况是这样的，在德雷达瓦大学——也就是此次疫情的中心，住进男生宿舍的学生有一半都病倒了。

sentences.en: The student clinic is overflowing with cases.
sentences.zh: 学生诊所里挤满了病例。

sentences.en: At first, they don't know what's wrong with these people.
sentences.zh: 起初，他们不知道这些人是怎么了。

sentences.en: And then they start to realize that they've got malaria.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始意识到，这些人感染了疟疾。

sentences.en: And eventually, more than 10,000 people are diagnosed with malaria in a city where, like, a half dozen people might get malaria in the course of the year normally.
sentences.zh: 最终，在一座平时一年可能只有区区六个人感染疟疾的城市里，有超过一万人被诊断出患有疟疾。

sentences.en: Like, they've just not seen anything like this before.
sentences.zh: 他们以前从未见过这样的情景。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: So it's very clearly the beginning of a new phase of Africa's relationship to malaria.
sentences.zh: 所以这很显然是非洲与疟疾关系进入新阶段的开始。

sentences.en: And it sounds like that is because of Steve.
sentences.zh: 听起来这都是因为斯蒂夫。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And I wanted to see what does it look like when Steven Zai invades a city?
sentences.zh: 我想看看当斯蒂芬·斯蒂芬森入侵一个城市时会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Why is that potentially such a problem?
sentences.zh: 为什么这可能是一个如此严重的问题？

sentences.en: And then I also wanted to see what cities, what health systems are able to do, if anything, when they're trying to respond.
sentences.zh: 然后我还想看看，当城市的卫生系统试图做出反应时，他们能够做些什么（如果有的话）。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Ethiopian government is not receptive to foreign journalists.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，埃塞俄比亚政府并不欢迎外国记者。

sentences.en: And it took me many, many months.
sentences.zh: 我花了整整好几个月的时间。

sentences.en: But finally, back in May, I got to Diradawa.
sentences.zh: 但最终，在五月份，我终于来到了德雷达瓦。

sentences.en: And I went to spend time with a couple of scientists, a molecular biologist named Fitzim Tedese and an entomologist named Ejeni Gattachu.
sentences.zh: 我去拜访了几位科学家，一位是名叫菲齐姆·特德塞的分子生物学家，另一位是名叫埃杰尼·加塔丘的昆虫学家。

sentences.en: And they've been studying Steven Zai and this outbreak since the moment it started.
sentences.zh: 从疫情爆发的那一刻起，他们就一直在研究斯蒂芬·斯蒂芬森和这次疫情。

sentences.en: Well, tell us more about this trip.
sentences.zh: 给我们多讲讲这次旅行吧。

sentences.en: So I got to Diradawa and it's a very, very hot, very arid city in a river valley.
sentences.zh: 我到了德雷达瓦，那是一个位于河谷中、非常非常炎热且干旱的城市。

sentences.en: It's very close to the border with Djibouti and Somalia.
sentences.zh: 它离吉布提和索马里的边境很近。

sentences.en: It's a very vibrant place, especially at night.
sentences.zh: 那是一个充满生机的地方，尤其是到了晚上。

sentences.en: It really comes alive at night because of the heat.
sentences.zh: 因为天气炎热，它在夜间真正活跃起来。

sentences.en: It has lots of little narrow streets and the houses are behind high walls.
sentences.zh: 那里有许多狭窄的小街道，房屋都隐藏在高墙后面。

sentences.en: It's very dense housing, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，那里的居住密度非常高。

sentences.en: Little blue auto rickshaws zip around in the street and you get women who are wearing really brightly colored hijab and robes.
sentences.zh: 蓝色的小型机动三轮车在街上呼啸而过，你会看到身穿色彩鲜艳的头巾和长袍的妇女。

sentences.en: And when I get there, basically the very first thing we do is we go to the place where these scientists, Fitzim and Dijene, first found Steven Zai.
sentences.zh: 当我到达那里时，基本上我们做的第一件事就是去那些科学家——菲齐姆和迪杰内——最初发现斯蒂芬·斯蒂芬森的地方。

sentences.en: Which is where?
sentences.zh: 那是哪里？

sentences.en: Okay, you've got the gear.
sentences.zh: 好了，装备你都带齐了。

sentences.en: I'm ready.
sentences.zh: 我准备好了。

sentences.en: Well, it's along the banks in little pools that have been left along the sides of the bank of the river that runs through Diradawa.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它就在穿城而过的德雷达瓦河两岸留下的一个个小水洼里。

sentences.en: I'm ready to meet my first Steven Zai.
sentences.zh: 我准备好去见我的第一个斯蒂芬·斯蒂芬森了。

sentences.en: I love a little stagnant water.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢死水了。

sentences.en: So we're standing in the shallow water on the edge of the river.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正站在河边的浅水中。

sentences.en: There are a lot of mosquito larvae here.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多蚊子幼虫。

sentences.en: Can you see this one?
sentences.zh: 你能看到这只吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 看到了。

sentences.en: It's moving.
sentences.zh: 它在动。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can see them.
sentences.zh: 对，我能看到它们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Dijene is scooping up water from these pools and puddles and looking at the larvae.
sentences.zh: 迪杰内正在这些水池和水坑里舀水，并观察着幼虫。

sentences.en: You would say the chances are very high at Steven Zai.
sentences.zh: 可以说这里出现斯蒂芬·斯蒂芬森的几率非常高。

sentences.en: Very, very high.
sentences.zh: 非常非常高。

sentences.en: And what he's trying to do when they collect samples in a place like this is figure out how much of the mosquito population is actually Steve.
sentences.zh: 当他们在这样的地方收集样本时，他试图弄清楚的是，在蚊群中究竟有多少比例是斯蒂夫。

sentences.en: And they started doing this next to the river when the malaria outbreak began because a lot of the initial cases that were reported were in families who lived near here,
sentences.zh: 疟疾疫情爆发时，他们开始在河边这样做，因为据报道，许多最初的病例都发生在住在离这儿不远的家庭中，

sentences.en: near the river.
sentences.zh: 就在河边附近。

sentences.en: So we had 100 meter radius for the larvae.
sentences.zh: 所以我们以幼虫为中心划定了100米的半径。

sentences.en: 100 meter radius of everywhere you found a case?
sentences.zh: 凡是发现病例的地方，周围100米半径都要查？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And what they do is they go to the home of everyone who's diagnosed with malaria and they trap the mosquitoes in and around the house.
sentences.zh: 他们的做法是去每个被诊断为疟疾的患者家中，把房子内外的蚊子都捕捉起来。

sentences.en: So, lo and behold, 97% of the mosquitoes they catch are Anopheles Steven Zai.
sentences.zh: 瞧，他们捕捉到的蚊子中有97%都是斯蒂芬按蚊。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So this mosquito is clearly thriving.
sentences.zh: 所以这种蚊子显然滋生得非常繁盛。

sentences.en: But is it mostly contained to the river?
sentences.zh: 但它主要只局限在河边吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是的。

sentences.en: So, in fact, they found Steve in a lot of other places that are a lot less predictable than a river.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们在许多其他地方也发现了斯蒂夫，这些地方比河流要难以预测得多。

sentences.en: The places this mosquito is turning up are really surprising if you think about the ways that we traditionally think of mosquitoes in Africa behaving.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑到我们传统上对非洲蚊子行为的认知，这种蚊子出现的地方真的很令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Steve is so adaptable that, sure, she'll breed in these pools next to the river, but she'll also breed in water tanks.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂夫的适应能力太强了，当然，她会在河边的这些水坑里繁殖，但她也会在水箱里繁殖。

sentences.en: And she can breed in the amount of water that you might find in an old bottle cap.
sentences.zh: 而且她甚至能在你从一个旧瓶盖里找到的那点儿水里繁殖。

sentences.en: She will feed on humans, yes, but she'll also feed on livestock.
sentences.zh: 她会吸食人类的血，是的，但她也会吸食家畜的血。

sentences.en: And that's why, actually, the next place that Dijene wanted to take me was into a goat shed.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，迪杰内想带我去的下一个地方其实是一个山羊棚。

sentences.en: So, lots of families in Diradawa have these little outbuildings in their homes where they keep a couple of goats or a couple of sheep, maybe a cow.
sentences.zh: 所以，德雷达瓦的许多家庭都在自家里建有这样的小附属建筑，用来养几只山羊、几只绵羊，或者一头牛。

sentences.en: And it turns out that the mosquito will rest in there because it's cool and it's dark and it's moist during the daytime when it's really hot.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，白天天气非常热的时候，蚊子会栖息在里面，因为那里凉爽、黑暗且潮湿。

sentences.en: And there's also, of course, a very accessible source of food.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然还有一个非常容易获取的食物来源。

sentences.en: Which is the goats.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些山羊。

sentences.en: The goats.
sentences.zh: 正是山羊。

sentences.en: So, I'm following along behind Dijene down these narrow alleyways.
sentences.zh: 于是，我跟在迪杰内身后走过这些狭窄的小巷。

sentences.en: Aha!
sentences.zh: 啊哈！

sentences.en: An animal shed with a low roof.
sentences.zh: 一个低矮屋顶的动物棚舍。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the next thing you know, he's down on his hands and knees crawling into these little buildings.
sentences.zh: 接下来，你会发现他已经双手双膝着地，爬进了这些小建筑物里。

sentences.en: They're maybe like three or four feet tall or crammed full of goats.
sentences.zh: 它们大概只有三四英尺高，里面挤满了山羊。

sentences.en: And in he goes and, you know, he wants to show me how this works.
sentences.zh: 他进去了，而且，你知道的，他想向我展示这是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: So, in I go too.
sentences.zh: 所以，我也进去了。

sentences.en: Okay, I am crawling into the goat shed.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我正爬进山羊棚。

sentences.en: Here we go.
sentences.zh: 我们进去了。

sentences.en: I can see nothing.
sentences.zh: 我什么也看不见。

sentences.en: I'm going to end up sitting on a goat.
sentences.zh: 我最后可能会坐到一只山羊身上。

sentences.en: I'm too tall.
sentences.zh: 我太高了。

sentences.en: I'm generally not made to be an entomologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我这身材通常不适合当昆虫学家。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hi, goats.
sentences.zh: 嗨，山羊们。

sentences.en: There are one, two, three, four, five, six, seven goats.
sentences.zh: 这里有一只、两只、三只、四只、五只、六只、七只山羊。

sentences.en: And he gets on his phone and he uses the flashlight to run it sort of really quickly over the walls.
sentences.zh: 他拿出手机，用手电筒在墙上飞快地照了一下。

sentences.en: And there were mosquitoes.
sentences.zh: 这里有蚊子。

sentences.en: What did we find?
sentences.zh: 我们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Fed mosquito.
sentences.zh: 吸过血的蚊子。

sentences.en: You can tell from out here?
sentences.zh: 你在外面就能看出来？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's black.
sentences.zh: 对，它是黑色的。

sentences.en: The abdomen is black.
sentences.zh: 腹部是黑色的。

sentences.en: Okay, all right.
sentences.zh: 好吧，原来如此。

sentences.en: To Jenny is able, in the dark, in the gloom, with the goats, to identify which mosquitoes they are.
sentences.zh: 迪杰内在黑暗、昏暗、伴随着山羊的环境中，能够辨别出它们是什么蚊子。

sentences.en: I can barely see them.
sentences.zh: 我几乎什么都看不见。

sentences.en: Oh, oh, oh, oh.
sentences.zh: 哦，哦，哦，哦。

sentences.en: Angry goat.
sentences.zh: 生气的山羊。

sentences.en: Sorry, goats.
sentences.zh: 对不起，山羊们。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 对不起。

sentences.en: He's, like, totally unfazed by the goats.
sentences.zh: 他似乎完全没有被这些山羊影响。

sentences.en: And when he sees the mosquitoes, what he does is he's got what's called an aspirator, which is like a little glass tube with a piece of rubber piping on the end.
sentences.zh: 当他看到蚊子时，他使用的是一种叫做吸蚊器的工具，它就像一个小玻璃管，端部连着一段橡胶管。

sentences.en: And he puts the rubber pipe in his mouth, and he holds the end of the glass tube up against the wall where he's seen a mosquito, and he gently sucks it in.
sentences.zh: 他把橡胶管含在嘴里，把玻璃管的一端贴在看到蚊子的墙壁上，然后轻轻一吸。

sentences.en: Got him.
sentences.zh: 抓住了。

sentences.en: So that it's alive, so that it's alive, but trapped.
sentences.zh: 这样它们还活着，活着但被捕获了。

sentences.en: And what they do is, again, like, take them back to the lab where they can sort them properly and identify which species it is,
sentences.zh: 他们的做法依然是把它们带回实验室，在那里进行正确分类并识别出是哪个物种，

sentences.en: and then know whether he's finding Steve in these places.
sentences.zh: 然后就能知道他在这些地方是否找到了斯蒂夫。

sentences.en: This is an amazing thing to envision.
sentences.zh: 想象一下这真是个惊人的画面。

sentences.en: Well, it's particularly amazing if you think about doing it with, like, a large herd of goats,
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你想到还要在一大群山羊中完成这件事，那就更惊人了，

sentences.en: who are also very interested in what's happening and are fully attempting to participate.
sentences.zh: 这些山羊对正在发生的事情也非常感兴趣，并且正全力试图参与进来。

sentences.en: These goats are spilling at me.
sentences.zh: 这些山羊快挤到我身上了。

sentences.en: Excuse me.
sentences.zh: 借过一下。

sentences.en: Pardon me.
sentences.zh: 对不起。

sentences.en: So when Dijenny had sucked all the visible mosquitoes off the walls, we crawled back out of the shed.
sentences.zh: 当迪杰内把墙上所有看得见的蚊子都吸走后，我们从棚子里爬了出来。

sentences.en: And walking through more of these narrow streets, I gotta tell you, like, I'm looking at the place on a whole new way now, right?
sentences.zh: 走在更多这样的狭窄街道上，我得告诉你，我现在是以一种全新的方式在看待这个地方，对吧？

sentences.en: And I'm just thinking there are so many places where Steve could be.
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，斯蒂夫可能存在的地方实在是太多了。

sentences.en: If you think that, like, she only needs small amounts of water to breed, and she's happy with artificial sources of water, she's happy in containers, in old plastic containers.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑到，比如说，她只需要少量的水就能繁殖，而且她对人工水源很满意，在容器里、在旧塑料容器里也能过得很好。

sentences.en: I'm looking around, and I'm seeing puddles under cisterns, and I'm seeing water storage containers in front of people's houses.
sentences.zh: 我四处张望，看到蓄水池下的水坑，看到人们家门前的储水容器。

sentences.en: Dhiradoa's municipal water only runs a couple of days a week, so when it turns on, everybody fills up some barrels, some jerry cans in front of their house, and keeps them nearby.
sentences.zh: 德雷达瓦的市政供水一周只来几天水，所以一来水，大家就会在房前灌满一些大桶、塑料水桶，并把它们放在身边。

sentences.en: And they don't have reliable trash collection, so you'll get lots of these little bits of plastic around that are a place for it to breed.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有可靠的垃圾收集服务，所以你会发现周围有很多这样的小塑料碎片，它们成了蚊子繁殖的场所。

sentences.en: And when we talk about Stevens Eye being a threat across Africa, like, that's one of the reasons why, right?
sentences.zh: 当我们谈到斯蒂芬按蚊对全非洲构成威胁时，这就是原因之一，对吧？

sentences.en: Because these erratic municipal services, it's a very common problem.
sentences.zh: 因为这些不规律的市政服务是一个非常普遍的问题。

sentences.en: So I'm looking around Dhiradoa, and I'm thinking, Steve could be everywhere here, and I'm thinking, like, the public health system is absolutely not in a state to respond to this.
sentences.zh: 所以我环顾德雷达瓦，心想斯蒂夫在这里可能无处不在，而且我觉得公共卫生系统绝对没有做好应对这一切的准备。

sentences.en: Well, what exactly is the public health infrastructure in a city like this that is now dealing with Steve and with so much malaria?
sentences.zh: 那么，在这样一个正面临着斯蒂夫和如此多疟疾肆虐的城市里，公共卫生基础设施到底是什么样的？

sentences.en: So Ethiopia has really been investing in primary care, in public health, but they don't have urban malaria response, right?
sentences.zh: 埃塞俄比亚确实一直在投资初级医疗和公共卫生，但他们没有应对城市疟疾的机制，对吧？

sentences.en: Remember, it hasn't been an urban disease, so there's no muscle memory in the city for responding.
sentences.zh: 记住，这过去并非一种城市疾病，所以城市里没有应对它的肌肉记忆。

sentences.en: People don't have immunity, they get very ill, and clinics don't know what they're looking at.
sentences.zh: 人们没有免疫力，病得很重，而诊所也不知道他们面对的是什么。

sentences.en: I talked to a woman, a nurse, who was pregnant when she got malaria.
sentences.zh: 我采访过一位女护士，她感染疟疾时怀着孕。

sentences.en: She got incredibly sick, but it was 10 days and, you know, a half dozen malaria tests before she got a confirmed diagnosis because nobody was looking for it.
sentences.zh: 她病得非常严重，但过了10天，做了大半打疟疾测试后，她才得到确诊，因为根本没有人去寻找这种病。

sentences.en: And this is a nurse who presumably has a lot of strong ties to the medical community.
sentences.zh: 而这是一个按理说与医疗界有着紧密联系的护士。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When you get a sudden severe malaria outbreak in a place that's not expecting it, it can really quickly start to derail things, right?
sentences.zh: 当你在一个毫无防备的地方突然遭遇严重的疟疾爆发时，事情很快就会开始脱轨，对吧？

sentences.en: And if you think that there are 600 million people who live in cities in Africa, then that's so many people who are potentially vulnerable to this mosquito.
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑到非洲城市里居住着六亿人口，那么有这么多人潜在地面临着这种蚊子的威胁。

sentences.en: So when you start to put all of those things together, you get the scenario that keeps Ethiopian scientists awake at night.
sentences.zh: 所以当你把所有这些情况放在一起时，就会出现让埃塞俄比亚科学家夜不能寐的场景。

sentences.en: That's really terrifying that CDC scientist who first told me about this.
sentences.zh: 最初向我讲述这一情况的疾控中心科学家对此感到非常恐惧。

sentences.en: And somewhat counterintuitively, we think of cities as places that represent progress and where health care is going to be better than in rural Africa.
sentences.zh: 而且有点违反直觉的是，我们认为城市代表着进步，那里的医疗保健会比农村地区更好。

sentences.en: You're saying that it's the opposite in this case.
sentences.zh: 你是说在这种情况下情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: The treatment is worse and the opportunities for the mosquitoes to grow are even greater.
sentences.zh: 治疗条件更差，而且蚊子滋生的机会甚至更大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Look, I don't think it's hopeless, right?
sentences.zh: 听着，我认为这并不是无可救药的，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't think that there's a reason why cities can't learn to respond to this, why people can't develop this expertise.
sentences.zh: 我不认为城市有什么理由学不会应对这一问题，人们有什么理由培养不出这种专业知识。

sentences.en: But it doesn't exist now.
sentences.zh: 但目前它并不存在。

sentences.en: Well, let's turn to the question of solutions, which is, Stephanie, the thing you set out to report on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我们转向解决方案的问题，这也是斯蒂芬妮你着手报道的内容。

sentences.en: Are there any?
sentences.zh: 有什么办法吗？

sentences.en: And not just solutions to Steve and African cities, but to the adaptations that are presenting such problems in rural Africa as well.
sentences.zh: 不仅是针对斯蒂夫和非洲城市的解决方案，还要应对那些在非洲农村地区也引发诸多问题的适应性变化。

sentences.en: What can African governments do about this beyond what they've already done?
sentences.zh: 除了已经做过的工作，非洲各国政府还能做些什么？

sentences.en: So there are some new solutions, and each one of them comes with some challenges.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有一些新的解决方案，但每一种方案都伴随着一些挑战。

sentences.en: First of all, there are improvements on the things we have.
sentences.zh: 首先，是对我们现有事物的改进。

sentences.en: There are new classes of insecticides being brought to market, and those will hopefully kill mosquitoes more effectively.
sentences.zh: 有新类别的杀虫剂正在推向市场，希望这些杀虫剂能更有效地杀死蚊子。

sentences.en: There's also some really interesting new innovative technologies.
sentences.zh: 还有一些非常有趣且创新的新技术。

sentences.en: I went to Kenya to see a clinical trial of something called a spatial repellent, which is this sheet of clear plastic.
sentences.zh: 我去了肯尼亚，观看了一种叫做空间驱蚊剂的临床试验，它是一张透明塑料薄膜。

sentences.en: It's about the size of a piece of loose leaf, and it's soaked in a repellent that confuses the mosquitoes, keeps them from being able to bite.
sentences.zh: 大约有一张活页纸那么大，浸泡在一种能让蚊子迷失方向、无法咬人的驱蚊剂中。

sentences.en: So the early indications are that both of these things are working really well.
sentences.zh: 所以早期的迹象表明，这两种方法都运作得非常好。

sentences.en: But our mosquitoes all the time are adapting, right?
sentences.zh: 但我们的蚊子一直在适应环境，对吧？

sentences.en: And so eventually, you're going to run into this question of resistance again.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，你还是会遇到这种耐药性的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: All these things sound like they ultimately have a shelf life.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西听起来最终都有保质期。

sentences.en: They can't last all that long, given just how quickly mosquitoes evolve and adapt.
sentences.zh: 考虑到蚊子进化和适应的速度之快，它们不可能维持太久。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's why you need to come at this from a couple of different directions, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么你需要从几个不同的方向来解决这个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's one of the places where I would say there's a lot of hope right now.
sentences.zh: 这也是我可以说目前存在很大希望的地方之一。

sentences.en: There's a new malaria vaccine that's being rolled out in sub-Saharan Africa.
sentences.zh: 撒哈拉以南非洲正在推广一种新的疟疾疫苗。

sentences.en: You give it to small children, and it should be able to provide them with a lot of protection throughout their lives.
sentences.zh: 把它给幼儿接种，应该能在他们的一生中提供大量的保护。

sentences.en: But, you know, vaccines, like we saw with COVID, they're challenging to deliver, and they can be expensive.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如我们在新冠疫情中看到的那样，疫苗分发起来很有挑战性，而且可能很昂贵。

sentences.en: They're coming in at about $10 per child, which maybe doesn't sound like so much.
sentences.zh: 它们的成本大约是每个孩子10美元，听起来可能不算太多。

sentences.en: But if you think about the fact that, for example, Tanzania, their whole health budget is $2 per person per year.
sentences.zh: 但如果你考虑到这样一个事实，例如坦桑尼亚，他们整个的卫生预算是每人每年2美元。

sentences.en: So stacks against that, these vaccines are really going to cost a lot.
sentences.zh: 因此与此相比，这些疫苗确实要花费巨资。

sentences.en: So the solution situation is not where anyone wants it to be.
sentences.zh: 所以解决方案的现状并不是任何人所期望的。

sentences.en: As you've been talking, Stephanie, it's occurred to me that we've spent this whole conversation talking about Africa.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬妮，听了你刚才的话，我突然想到我们整场对话都在谈论非洲。

sentences.en: But Steve seemed to come from outside of Africa to Africa, and now it's Africa's problem.
sentences.zh: 但斯蒂夫似乎是从非洲以外来到非洲的，现在这成了非洲的问题。

sentences.en: I have to assume that a fear might be that as malaria becomes a bigger and bigger crisis in Africa, for all the reasons we're talking about here,
sentences.zh: 我不得不假设，人们可能会担心，由于我们这里谈到的种种原因，随着疟疾在非洲成为越来越大的危机，

sentences.en: Africa could export its malaria problem to somewhere else in the world.
sentences.zh: 非洲可能会将它的疟疾问题输出到世界上的其他地方。

sentences.en: Is that what the scientists you talk to fear?
sentences.zh: 你交谈过的科学家们是否担心这一点？

sentences.en: You know, I think I would say it's not so much about export.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得这不是输出的问题。

sentences.en: It's not about something that comes on a boat.
sentences.zh: 这不是关于乘船运来的东西。

sentences.en: It's actually, it's about something much bigger than that.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这关系到比这大得多的事情。

sentences.en: What we've been seeing with mosquito-borne disease in the last few years is a really big impact from climate change.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年中，我们在蚊媒疾病上看到的是气候变化带来的巨大影响。

sentences.en: Lots of places are becoming a better environment for mosquitoes that carry a lot of different diseases, not just malaria.
sentences.zh: 许多地方正在成为携带各种疾病的蚊子的更好栖息地，不仅仅是疟疾。

sentences.en: I think what we're seeing is that in a very quickly changing world, mosquitoes do better, move faster than we do.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们看到的是，在一个瞬息万变的世界里，蚊子比我们适应得更好、行动得更快。

sentences.en: And for me, that's the lesson from Steve that I saw in Ethiopia.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就是我在埃塞俄比亚从斯蒂夫身上看到的教训。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Not that Steve's going to leave Africa and come to other parts of the world, invade other continents,
sentences.zh: 不是说斯蒂夫要离开非洲去世界其他地方、入侵其他大陆，

sentences.en: but that the environmental issues that are present in a place like Africa are present elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 而是像非洲这样地方存在的环境问题，在其他地方也存在。

sentences.en: That's the problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: That, as humans, we create lots of situations where mosquitoes can flourish.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，作为人类，我们制造了许多让蚊子大量繁殖的环境。

sentences.en: They look different in different places, cities and towns, Africa versus Latin America.
sentences.zh: 它们在不同的地方看起来不同，城市和城镇，非洲对阵拉丁美洲。

sentences.en: But what those places have in common is that mosquitoes are thriving and posing a threat that we're not nearly quick enough in providing solutions for.
sentences.zh: 但这些地方的共同点是，蚊子正在滋生，并构成了威胁，而我们提供解决方案的速度远远不够快。

sentences.en: Or, it sounds like from the case of Africa, prepared to deal with in real time.
sentences.zh: 或者，从非洲的情况来看，没有准备好实时应对。

sentences.en: No, not yet.
sentences.zh: 不，还没有。

sentences.en: I think for me, the lesson of what I saw in Diridawa, what's happened with Steve, is really just how quickly things can go south, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为对我来说，我在迪雷达瓦看到的、斯蒂夫身上发生的事情给我的教训，其实就是事情可以多快地急转直下，对吧？

sentences.en: You can think that you don't have the problem, or you can think that you have the problem managed, or that you have the tools you need.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为你没有这个问题，或者你认为你已经控制了这个问题，或者你有所需的工具。

sentences.en: And the way mosquitoes work, incredibly quickly, you can find yourself with a public health crisis.
sentences.zh: 而根据蚊子的活动方式，快得难以置信，你就会发现自己陷入了公共卫生危机。

sentences.en: And I think as we think about the spread of mosquitoes and the threat they pose, I think that should be alarming for everybody.
sentences.zh: 我认为当我们思考蚊子的蔓延以及它们构成的威胁时，这应该对每个人敲响警钟。

sentences.en: Well, Stephanie, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，斯蒂芬妮，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感激。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 不用谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 从今天开始游玩。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: When I ran for president, I vowed to fix our broken student loan program.
sentences.zh: 当我竞选总统时，我发誓要修复我们破产的学生贷款计划。

sentences.en: Because while a college degree is still the ticket to a better life, that ticket has become excessively expensive.
sentences.zh: 因为虽然大学学位仍然是通往更好生活的门票，但这张票已经变得过于昂贵。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, President Biden canceled $9 billion more in student loan debt, just as requirements to repay those loans, which have been paused for three years, have resumed.
sentences.zh: 周三，拜登总统又取消了90亿美元的学生贷款债务，而这些已经暂停了三年的贷款的还款要求刚刚恢复。

sentences.en: Biden's previous attempts to forgive a far larger amount of student loans were struck down by the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 拜登先前试图免除更大金额学生贷款的尝试被最高法院驳回。

sentences.en: But the latest effort is a workaround that relies on a different law.
sentences.zh: 但最新的努力是一种依靠不同法律的变通方法。

sentences.en: As I said at the time, I believe the court's decision to strike down my student debt relief program is wrong.
sentences.zh: 正如我当时所说，我认为法院驳回我的学生债务减免计划的决定是错误的。

sentences.en: But I promised I wouldn't give up.
sentences.zh: 但我承诺我不会放弃。

sentences.en: And more than 75,000 employees of the health care company Kaiser Permanente began a three-day strike on Wednesday,
sentences.zh: 医疗保健公司凯撒永久（Kaiser Permanente）的75000多名员工于周三开始为期三天的罢工，

sentences.en: becoming the latest group of unionized workers to walk off the job in the past few months.
sentences.zh: 成为过去几个月中最新罢工的工会工人群体。

sentences.en: The workers are demanding higher wages, which they say are necessary to end labor shortages that have plagued the company for years.
sentences.zh: 工人们要求提高工资，他们称这是结束困扰该公司多年的劳动力短缺所必需的。

sentences.en: The strike is being closely watched because Kaiser Permanente's health care plans cover 13 million Americans across eight states.
sentences.zh: 这场罢工正受到密切关注，因为凯撒永久的医疗保健计划覆盖了八个州的1300万美国人。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Alex Stern, Will Reed, Rob Zipko, and Sidney Harper.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由亚历克斯·斯特恩（Alex Stern）、威尔·里德（Will Reed）、罗布·齐普科（Rob Zipko）和西德尼·哈珀（Sidney Harper）制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.

sentences.en: Davis Lynn, contains original music by Rowan Emisto, Marion Lozano, and Dan Powell, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯·林恩（Davis Lynn）剪辑，包含罗文·埃米斯托（Rowan Emisto）、马里昂·洛扎诺（Marion Lozano）和丹·鲍威尔（Dan Powell）的原创音乐，并由艾莉莎·莫克斯利（Alyssa Moxley）进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由来自Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格（Jim Brunberg）和本·兰斯福德（Ben Lansford）创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Baro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴罗（Michael Baro）。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让您的客人在家里感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是全黑睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否黑屏晕倒去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢收听的任何地方找到《Wirecutter秀》。
